title: Beginning game dev
author: DisabilitySos_
selftext: I am looking for some advice for game dev. I just don't know where to start. I have a really good Mac (M4, 128gb) I want to make mobile and multi format games in the kirosoft/game stew genre. I need advice on engine, ai local or frontier. I am happy to learn and spend.

comments.author: hyphen_ai
comments.body: Go with Godot and Claude, ChatGPT or Grok are all good.

comments.author: forgingtheflow
comments.body:
My experience has put Claude as the best for coding by a long shot. That’s based on using ChatGPT Astra and getting nowhere with an issue, then trying Claude opus 5.5 and fixing the issue plus finding 40+ other issues all in the same day. I use ChatGPT for artwork and voice work, so I use both.   
As for where to start, pick an AI and give it as detailed brief as you can and it’ll let you know how and where to begin.

replies.author: forgingtheflow
replies.body: Well ChatGPT hasn’t needed anything else. Take a look at my landing page, all built with ChatGPT, all in-game assets, everything; http://forgedflow.com/red-sol/

comments.author: Orlandogameschool
comments.body:
I would start with free models like google ai studio it comes with free game demos you can just prompt and remix  https://aistudio.google.com/welcome 

Then it just depends on what you wanna do or make. I would start making basic games first on the free plans of Claude and chat gpt

comments.author: SadMangonel
comments.body: Actually talk this through with Claude. It knows exactly what to do.

replies.author: BloodMossHunter
replies.body: This. Ask claude everything like hes your priest and friend

comments.author: Mubeenization
comments.body: Watch Bitemegames and Creauctopus Youtube channels. You'll get way ahead.

comments.author: Beskull
comments.body:
Dude, just get a coding system, like Claude or codex, and detail the main points of your game, and have it build it. 
Don't go engine yet. Just have it build a web game. This way you can refine the design, and learn how to build with ai agents

comments.author: No_Thanks_7089
comments.body:
Claude and Godot is your best bet but if you want to do it locally. You'll get good speed with Qwen 3.8 27b and maybe flash next (Q4 being 100ish GB). Its not as good for anything complicated, open ended or vague. I'd be using Claude for most of it but you could get Claude to output work to your local machine. I like unsloth but not sure about how it goes on Mac.

Using your Mac to do grunt work will save usage on Claude but only if you make sure Claude knows to only give it basic work and output detailed briefs for it to follow.

I've just started 3 weeks ago myself and found Claude + one month of free Chatgpt is a good combo. Gpt does my art and I get it to do huge research and compile data as it's free using the chat on high rather than codex.(For now, abuse it while you can.)

comments.author: je386
comments.body:
You can do multiplatform games with kotlin multiplatform/compose multiplatform, which is very similar to android development, but for all platforms (android, iOS, web with webassembly (wasm) and desktop (anything that runs a JVM, so windows, mac, linux, BSD and more).

But you also can use one of the gaming frameworks like godot, but I cannot tell anything about these, because I don't use them.

For development, claude or github copilot coding agent with claude is fine.  
I have both inside my intelliJ.

Also, with a M4 mac, you could try if a local model works for smaller tasks. There is a ollama plugin for intelliJ which can connect to a local running instance of Qwen.  
I only tested a very small model and it was not helpful, but my maschine has no big GPU, they may work on your maschine

comments.author: Any-Blacksmith-2054
comments.body: Godot + Blender mcp + Opus 5.5 in $20 subscription (free chatgpt only for concept arts)
